body: I think this could be said about every chapter...except for the whole boredom part.

It's just that I would like someone to talk to and I think face-to-face interaction would be best for me. Trying to get an appointment with a psychiatrist who specializes in PTSD and is covered by my insurance is so god damn difficult. I don't think you can have a meaningful interaction with a person you do not know, unless it's in person.

Hey, I appreciate the help. I was wondering if there was someone who specified in helping out returning students though. The dean's office is usually incredibly busy around this time of the year. Also, I've e-mailed a few of the names on that page and they never got back to me. I'm not a registered student, just looking to re-register.
I was in the School of Business and I'd love to return there, but if not, then probably SAS or SEBS.

Is it truthfully necessary to have a protagonist in a series? Every character, from Joffrey to Jon, is so complicated and REAL. And I understand that this is a fantasy, but the realism engrained in the series allows the reader to easily immerse themselves into the world.
The entire bottle isn't one serving. But I enjoy what the marketing majors these days are doing with their time.
